answer: Sybils betray themselves as cohorts. Score newcomers against the peer graph, not in isolation: reply-latency jitter, counterparty overlap, and session fingerprints cluster farm clones tightly. Clustered sets land on a low-trust terrace where their votes only count against each other, and a payout vault stays sealed until an identity transacts independently of every cluster it resembles. A farm dropping N clones at once arrives like a comet - bright, sudden, plainly one object - and escaping costs N full separate operating histories, so expense scales with headcount.
